head: fe23373217468a098d53dbda188eabc500d3c3c9
classification_reasons: Blast radius: about 30 plugin, template and test files; the gate record gains a new `proof` entry in every (c), (d) and (e) record and a fourth `runs` key; `DEFERRABLE_CHECKS`, `red_targets`, `limits.run_caps` and `run_phase.py` (port-list lines) change: a record shape and contract change across the runner's step, the round and the PR body.

Spec tightness: acceptance is measurable (figures 245/250, 185/190, 355, 180/185 asserted; per-behaviour tests), but three flagged concerns are design guesses for the panel, and the `proof` entry's shape is declared provisional pending R11.
Test coverage: the new paths (drive run, proof judgment, (b) item check, (e) cap subtraction, collect.py drive, stale-proof line) have no existing tests; every Proof test is still to be written.
attempted: Intent: every Proposed outcome bullet maps to a spec requirement (R1 drive key and env, R2 runner step at c/d/e and by-hand collect.py, R3 apart from the three targets, R4 job time, R5 grammar, R6 manifest, R7 proof entry and rounds, R8 image caps, R9 gate (b) refusal, R10 /sdlc-init Playwright, R11 four-log lists and skill texts, R12 PR line, R13 triage, R14 two folders, R15 commands and agents, R16 version). One small drift, not a reason: the intent lists `commands_summary` among the readers that learn the drive; the spec keeps it unchanged (it reports only the `commands` and `evidence` entries, so the drive shows in the commands reason but the `proof` verdict is absent from the run's JSON summary).

Spec and plan: every requirement has a file and an order-of-work step; the earlier reviews' five escalation points are closed in this HEAD (fix round at (e) is 290 with and without a drive and consistent with the subtraction; both policy SKILL.md files and the ux check message are in the plan; `evidence_status` gains `root` and all three callers are listed, including `release/notes.py _evidence_line`; `run_caps`/`run_timeout_seconds` gain `gate_phase` with the two call sites; four callers of `limits.run_caps`). Diff contains only the change folder (spec, plan, status, evidence), as a design run should.

Claims against today's code, run_phase.py: `commands_timeout_seconds` is 3 x command_timeout + 5 min (line 2271-2278; default 900 s => 50 min); `build_caps_minutes_needed` = build wall clock 180 + grace 5 + commands + judge 10 = 245 (lines 352-362); `run_caps(config, phase, env)` and `run_timeout_seconds` exist as described (391-405); call sites are line 2082 (`--max-turns`) and 3333 (`invoke`) as the plan says; `gate_phase = st.phase if phase == 'fix'` at 3106; `commands_env()` strips credentials and tokens (2367-2382); `commit_run_record` follows the step (3620-3633). Arithmetic verified: with a 300 s drive the step is 55 min, build/fix 250 of 260, test 190 of 200, deploy (120-5)+5+55+10+125+45 = 355, triage +5 = 360, fix round at (e) 45+180+55+10 = 290 (today 45+185+50+10 = 290).

Claims, limits.py: `run_caps(gate_settings, build)` is the one copy read by the runner and `check_limits` (line 502); defaults 120 and 180; four callers confirmed (run_phase.run_caps, build_caps_minutes_needed, check_limits, sdlc_init.keep_build_caps at line 267). A fix round at (e) carries `run: build` and ctx.phase e, so runner (fix, gate_phase e) and gate subtract the same minutes, as the plan's Risks say.

Claims, gate.py: `DEFERRABLE_CHECKS = ('commands', 'evidence')` (389); `not_started`, `deferred_logs`, `write_deferred_logs(all_targets=phase in HEADER_REQUIRED_AT)` and the replace-only-pending rule (610-613) are as the spec describes; the intent's statement that (c) writes only marked logs is true. Re-judging `evidence` whenever a log is written (593) means a drive at (c) also re-judges evidence at (c): harmless since drive.log is optional there.

Claims, checks.py: `commands_from_config` reads build/test/lint only (267-277); `missing_targets` names the three; `run_command` runs the platform shell with `env` replaceable; `judge_targets` summary format matches 'drive (exit n)'; `check_evidence` reads `REQUIRED_EVIDENCE` and `COMMAND_LOGS`; `GateContext.approved_artifact` reads the merge base or fast-lane commit (135-146); `CHECKS_BY_PHASE['b']` includes `check_commands`, so the runner's step does run at (b): the spec's 'never at (b)' must be an explicit phase guard in `run_deferred_commands` (observation for the build: the Proof list tests c/d/e but no test pins that (b) runs no drive).

Claims, auto_round.py: `red_targets` today returns None as soon as `commands` is ok (line 114) and maps logs through `EVIDENCE_TARGETS` (146); a drive that exits 0 with a `differs` item therefore needs `red_targets` restructured, which the spec's 'a failed proof entry contributes one red entry' requires and the auto_round test covers. `head_matches` body (295-318) is what `only_change_folder_moved` lifts, renames counted via --no-renames. `JUDGE_PROMPT`, `REQUEST_TEXT`, `targets_summary`, `red_targets_request` exist as named.

Claims, readers: `description.evidence_status(change_dir, phase)` (239) counts every file in screenshots/ including .gitkeep (true); `LOG_FILES` at 79; `_auto_round_line` renders `exit {exit_code}` (would print 'exit None' for a proof target, as the spec says); callers at description.py:758, pr/cli.py:236 (`check_run_result` holds root), release/notes.py:156 (`build_notes` holds root). `triage.logs_for` adds the three logs on a failed `commands` (139). `collect.py` TARGETS, CI deferral and `ensure_screenshots_dir` match; `run_drive(ctx, ...)` will need a GateContext built in collect.py (implementation detail).

Claims, init and templates: `detect.node_dependencies` exists (593) reading both blocks; `Target`, `_no_target`, `Detection.setup`, `as_dict` as described; `sdlc_init` has `--setup` and `SETUP_CMD`; `template/sdlc.yaml` has commands build/test/lint/setup/env and `deploy.command: ""`; `commands.env` reaches the runner via the workflow env and so the drive inherits it through `commands_env()`. The four workflow templates' timeout comments state 185/245 and 355 as the spec reads them.

Claims, skills and commands: definition-of-done SKILL.md:60-63 and ux-conventions SKILL.md:44-53 say no gate check requires a screenshot; ux check.py globs evidence/* directly (so today it misses evidence/screenshots/, which this change fixes); sdlc-test.md:83-84 carries the 'evidence missing' sentence no code backs; sdlc-build.md:93 names the screenshot in Proof; verifier.md step 2 names the tree. All as the spec states.

Decisions: 2 (plan approved at (b), gate reads the approved copy) kept by judging the merge-base plan; 29 (red target a round, timeout a round, infrastructure one re-run then park, missing target parks) followed, with one small deviation the spec chose deliberately: a missing manifest parks without the re-run decision 29 gives infrastructure failures; 19, 21/37 (state items deterministic, never panel items) and 35 (banner stays the risk list's) kept.
Proof: at (b) there is no toolchain log; the Proof section names a test file per behaviour and states every test is still to be written; the acceptance figures are concrete and assertable.

Blast radius: no guardrail file in the diff; root sdlc.yaml and workflows untouched. Readers of `deferred_commands` (release/cli.py:813, merge_step.py:355, run_phase.py 1823/2398/5002) automatically treat a still-deferred `proof` entry as not passed, which is fail-closed; their messages name only commands/evidence (cosmetic, not in the plan).

Policies: security-baseline rule 3/7 (no credential, no network allowance added; drive output lands where target output already lands); rule 2 observation for the build: the spec requires screenshot items under evidence/proof/ but does not say a `state:` or `screenshot:` path is resolved and kept inside proof/ (`..` or a symlink the drive writes); the drive itself already runs session code with the same environment and its output already lands in the record, so this adds no new capability, but a resolve-and-contain check is cheap. Data-conventions rules 1, 4, 6 applied (manifest names commit and run; additive record change). Risk list: no item touched, consistent with risk-hits {}.

Tests: pre-existing tests are extended, not weakened (change type feature; plan says text tests are updated with the texts, step tests stay untouched); the planned tests would fail with the bug present for each behaviour listed (stale-proof line has both sides pinned, fix round at (e) figure asserted). Gap noted above: no test for 'no drive at (b)'.
